submission.natural_language_explanation: Retrospective nominal-anchor head: it rests attending to the first token and diverts to lock onto a salient mid-sentence nominal anchor, typically an event/outcome noun (controversy, clashes, pressure, differences, results, evidence, agreement) or the detached single-letter initial ' B' of a proper name, firing on the anchor itself via self-attention or on the function word right after it (that/a/have/,/does) attending back; ordinary concrete nouns (cat, dog), common full-form surnames (Smith) and other single letters (C) stay at rest.

rival_explanations: Broader: it is a generic subject/noun-phrase head firing on any subject noun or its follower, so concrete nouns like cat, dog and Smith will test active given enough context.
Narrower: it is a memorized unigram/bigram detector for items like take+that, took+a and space-B with no class generalization, so unseen event nouns such as turmoil or upheaval will test inactive.
